method: Each named route checked live against the vendor's own pricing/terms page (first-party read where the page serves static content; dated third-party reads of the vendor's own page where the vendor page is JS-rendered or the row has aged off). No account created, no key provisioned, no payment made. A route counts as verified-free API capacity only if the vendor's own published terms state a standing $0 API tier. One-off signup/trial credits, consumer-app free use, and reseller credit hosts are not API capacity.
net_reading: Zero of the six claimed $0 routes verify as free API capacity. One route is discontinued (Sora 2), three are paid-only on the vendor's own pricing page (MiniMax, NanoBanana, Wan 2.6), and the two verified-free entries (SadTalker, Gamma) are not API routes at all. Nothing in this catalogue is wired into Inference routing: every entry has wired=false, and the test suite (Inference/tests/test_inf042_free_tier_routes.py) fails if any verified-free entry is ever an API route or if any entry is marked wired. A verdict changes only on a new dated first-party read; re-check triggers are named per route in docs/collaboration/TASK-INF-042-FREE-TIER-ROUTE-CATALOGUE.md.

findings: OpenAI notified developers 2026-03-24 that the Videos API and every Sora 2 alias/snapshot would be removed from the API on 2026-09-24; the Sora consumer app and website closed 2026-04-26 (OpenAI Help Center).

Live read of the OpenAI deprecations page 2026-11-25 returns zero matches for 'sora': the row has aged off the table now that the shutdown is past; the table lists only shutdowns from Dec 2026 onward.

Four dated third-party reads (8frame 2026-10-02, soku.ai 2026-10-21, layer3labs, kenerateai) quote the same OpenAI deprecation text and the model-page banner: 'The Sora 2 models and Videos API were shut down on September 24, 2026 and are no longer available. No one-to-one replacement API is available.' The replacement column was empty for every Sora row.
While live, the API charged $0.10/second (sora-2, 720p) and $0.30-$0.70/second (sora-2-pro); the app had a free tier with daily limits. Both are history.

routes.verdict_detail: discontinued — no free tier, no paid tier, no route at any price
routes.vyralx_implication: No Sora 2 generation option exists. Any VyralX material still naming Sora 2 as a route is stale.

routes.candidate_spec_state: Stays BLOCKED_NO_CREDENTIALS, spec-only, no provider adapter — and the free-tier premise in its notes is now disproven by this verdict. Wiring is conditional on a verified first-party free tier, which does not exist.

findings: Live first-party read of platform.minimax.io/docs/pricing/overview, 2026-11-25: the page states no free tier and no free credits anywhere. Pay-as-you-go billing: 'API usage charges are deducted from your account balance' after funds are added.

MiniMax-M3 $0.30 in / $1.20 out per 1M tokens (<=512k input, permanent 50% off); MiniMax-M3.1-Flash $0.15 in / $0.60 out. TTS speech-2.8-turbo $60 / M characters, speech-2.8-hd $100 / M characters; ASR $0.38/hour. Audio Packages from $5/month (100,000 points).
The only free allowances printed on the pricing page are input-side: the first 5 input images per video task are free, and audio input is free. Neither is a free tier for the API.

The M Plan $0 tier is the MiniMax Code agent app (limited M3.1 Flash use, no API key for other tools, no H3 video) — not API capacity. A third-party aggregator's June 2026 claim of a ¥15 signup credit is contradicted by two November 2026 reads of the first-party page and is not a standing tier.
Corroborated by independent reads of the same first-party page dated 2026-10-24 and 2026-11-17.

routes.verdict_detail: no free API tier on the vendor's own pricing page; pay-as-you-go from a funded balance
routes.vyralx_implication: MiniMax is not a free voice/audio route for VyralX. TTS via MiniMax would be a paid integration and is out of scope under the free-only rule.

findings: Live first-party read of the Gemini Developer API pricing page, 2026-11-25, section 'Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (Nano Banana)': Free Tier reads 'Not available' for input price and output price on Standard, Batch, Flex and Priority tabs. Paid: $0.30 per 1M input tokens, $0.039 per image output (1,290 tokens per 1024px-class image).
The model is deprecated on Google's own page: 'Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (gemini-2.5-flash-image) is deprecated and will be shut down on March 15, 2027; migrate to Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image.'

The newer family members (Nano Banana 2.1, 2, 2 Lite, Pro) are listed the same way by independent readers of the same page (Nov 2026): Free Tier 'Not available' for all of them. Free use exists only inside Google's consumer apps (Gemini app, Flow, AI Studio) — not API capacity.

routes.verdict_detail: Gemini API Free Tier is 'Not available' for every Nano Banana model
routes.vyralx_implication: No free Nano Banana API route for VyralX image generation. Consumer-app use is a human workflow, not a pipeline input.

findings: Direct read of create.wan.video/pricing attempted 2026-11-25 and failed: the page is JS-rendered and returns 'Something went wrong' to a static fetch. The figures below are dated third-party reads of Alibaba's own pages, consistent across three independent readers.

Alibaba Cloud Model Studio pricing (read 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-25): wan2.6-t2v / wan2.6-i2v cost $0.10/second at 720p and $0.15/second at 1080p in the Singapore region; a 50-second free quota per model, valid 90 days, for new users in Singapore only. A trial quota that expires is not a standing free tier.

wan.video consumer site (read 2026-11-03): Free plan $0/month — daily check-in to earn credits, one video at a time, watermark on exports, testing use only, no commercial licence. Credit cost per clip is not published on the page.
Wan 2.6 has no public weights (Wan 2.2 is the last generation with downloadable weights), so there is no self-hosted route for this version.
Third-party credit hosts (VdoBloom via KIE, wanai.dev) sell credits for Wan 2.6 renders; they are resellers, not a first-party free tier, and are not capacity under the free-only rule.

routes.verdict_detail: no standing free API tier; a one-off 50-second new-user trial quota (Singapore, 90 days) is not a free tier
routes.vyralx_implication: No free Wan 2.6 API route for VyralX cinematic generation. The 50-second trial quota cannot carry a production line.

findings: Live first-party read of github.com/OpenTalker/SadTalker, 2026-11-25: public repo, 14,220 stars, 288 commits, main branch, CVPR 2023. README states the licence is Apache 2.0 with the non-commercial restriction removed; GitHub's own licence detector reports NOASSERTION for the repo — the discrepancy is recorded here, the README text is the claim.

The README states the code 'runs completely offline and does not collect any personal information or other data.' No hosted service, no API, no price. Checkpoints are downloaded separately (GitHub Releases / Google Drive / Baidu).
Requirements from the repo: Python 3.8+, PyTorch with CUDA (GPU recommended, CPU possible), FFmpeg. Output 256/512px face renders, head-only animation from one portrait + audio.

routes.vendor: OpenTalker (Xi'an Jiaotong University / Tencent AI Lab)
routes.verdict_detail: free open-source software; no hosted tier and no API, so not a routable provider
routes.vyralx_implication: SadTalker is free software, not a service. A VyralX avatar leg built on it would be a local-GPU pipeline component needing its own evaluation (hardware, quality, likeness rules) — not Inference fallback capacity, and not claimed here.

findings: Live first-party read of gamma.app/pricing, 2026-11-25: a Free plan is listed at $0 with 'No credit card required' — up to 10 slides per prompt; simple presentations, docs, websites, social and images; import from PDF and PPTX; export to PDF, PPTX, PNG and Google Slides.

The 400 one-time-credit figure is reported by multiple third-party reads of the same page (Nov 2026) and was not visible in the live crawl's dynamic slots — recorded as reported, not first-hand. Credits do not refresh; free decks carry Gamma branding.
API access is a Pro feature ($18/month billed annually) per the vendor's plan comparison — there is no free API tier. Gamma is a presentations surface, outside Inference's provider pool in any case.

routes.verdict_detail: standing $0 consumer plan verified; no free API tier, so not a routable provider
routes.vyralx_implication: None for video generation. Gamma's free plan is a real $0 plan for human-made decks, not pipeline capacity.
